question: In which year did the Non-Cooperation Movement begin in India?
solution:
Correct answer is __**1920.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Noncooperation was accepted to by the **Indian National Congress at Calcutta** in **September 1920** and started that December.
 
• The movement was actually **a peaceful and non-violent protest against the British government in India**.
 
• Indians were asked to **give up their titles and leave from nominated seats in the local bodies** as a mark of protest.
 
• **Middle class people** mainly take part in non cooperation movement in towns. 
 
• [IMAGE: https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcRhl_9cDSGQrJ9j94Dt6gSReriZALOkLTMTNg&usqp=CAU] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Civil disobedience, also known as passive resistance, **the refusal to obey the demands or commands of a government or occupying power, without resorting to violence or active measures of opposition**​.
 
• Gandhi organised** Kheda movement** to support farmers of the Kheda district.
 
• The **Champaran Satyagraha** is considered to be a important event in the history of India's freedom struggle.
